desc: Implement right-endpoint sweep: bucket pairs by larger value, activate all pairs with max==r before counting, track frequency map of lower-endpoint values and the top two distinct values (0 default) with owner of the unique max.
At each r add r - max_active to base count; if the max lower-endpoint value has frequency 1, credit (max - second_distinct) to that owner's removal gain, else credit 0.
Return base + max gain over all pairs, ensuring O(n + m) time and correct handling of duplicates/ties.
Execute the code on the two provided examples and confirm outputs 9 and 12 (print actual returned values) — verified PASS.
Brute-force cross-check on many small random n and conflictingPairs (duplicates, reversed pairs, single pair, irrelevant pairs) vs per-deletion recomputation — all matched.
